<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
  Let $t\geq 1$ be fixed. For every sufficiently large $n$, there exists an
  explicit binary $t$-edit correcting code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$
  with redundancy
  \[
    (2t+1)\log n+2t\log\log n+O_t(1),
  \]
  whose encoder and decoder run in polynomial time with respect to block-length $n$. Moreover,
  all but $O_t(\log n)$ message bits appear unaltered as the first
  $n-O_t(\log n)$ symbols of each codeword.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is a \emph{$t$-edit correcting code}
if $\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{c})\cap\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{c}')=\emptyset$ for all
distinct $\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}'\in\mathcal{C}$. Its \emph{redundancy} is
$n-\log|\mathcal{C}|$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:dist}
A code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is a $t$-edit correcting code if and
only if $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\geq 2t+1$ for all distinct
$\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}'\in\mathcal{C}$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
If $\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{c})\cap\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{c}')$,
then $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\leq 2t$ by the triangle inequality.
Conversely, if $d=d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\leq 2t$, apply the
first $\lceil d/2\rceil$ edits of a shortest edit sequence from $\mathbf{c}$
to $\mathbf{c}'$. The resulting word $\mathbf{y}$ satisfies
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{y})\leq\lceil d/2\rceil\leq t$ and
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{y},\mathbf{c}')\leq\lfloor d/2\rfloor\leq t$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:ball}
Let $\mathbf{u}\in\{0,1\}^\ell$ and $r\geq 0$. Then
\[
  |\mathcal{E}_r(\mathbf{u})|\leq (r+1)\big(4(\ell+r)+2\big)^r .
\]
Moreover, $\mathcal{E}_r(\mathbf{u})$ can be enumerated (possibly with
repetitions) in time $O\big((r+1)(4(\ell+r)+2)^r(\ell+r)\big)$. In particular,
if $\ell\leq n$ and $n\geq r+1$, then
$|\mathcal{E}_r(\mathbf{u})|\leq (r+1)(8n)^r$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Every word of $\mathcal{E}_r(\mathbf{u})$ is obtained from $\mathbf{u}$ by a
sequence of $j\leq r$ edits. Before each edit, the current word has length
$L\leq \ell+r$, and there are at most $2(L+1)+L+L=4L+2$ possible edits on it
(an insertion of one of two symbols at one of $L+1$ places, a deletion, or a
substitution at one of $L$ places). Hence there are at most
$(4(\ell+r)+2)^j$ sequences of exactly $j$ edits, and summing over
$j\in[0,r]$ gives the bound. Enumerating all such sequences and applying each
of them costs $O(\ell+r)$ time per sequence. Finally, if $\ell\leq n$ and
$n\geq r+1$, then $4(\ell+r)+2\leq 4n+4r+2\leq 8n$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:suffix}
Let $\mathbf{p},\mathbf{p}'\in\{0,1\}^m$ and
$\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s}'\in\{0,1\}^N$. If
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{p}\mathbf{s},\mathbf{p}'\mathbf{s}')\leq r$, then
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s}')\leq r$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
If $m=0$ there is nothing to prove, so let $m\geq 1$. Fix an alignment of
$\mathbf{p}\mathbf{s}$ and $\mathbf{p}'\mathbf{s}'$ of cost $c\leq r$, and
cut it right after the column that contains the $m$-th symbol of
$\mathbf{p}\mathbf{s}$, i.e., the last symbol of $\mathbf{p}$. By (F2), this
splits the alignment into an alignment of $\mathbf{p}$ and
$(\mathbf{p}'\mathbf{s}')_{[1,j]}$ of cost $c_1$, and an alignment of
$\mathbf{s}$ and $\mathbf{g}=(\mathbf{p}'\mathbf{s}')_{[j+1,m+N]}$ of cost
$c_2$, for some $j$, where $c_1+c_2=c$. By (F1), $c_1\geq|m-j|$. If $j\geq m$,
then $\mathbf{g}=\mathbf{s}'_{[j-m+1,N]}$, which is obtained from $\mathbf{s}'$
by deleting its first $j-m$ symbols. If $j<m$, then
$\mathbf{g}=\mathbf{p}'_{[j+1,m]}\mathbf{s}'$, which is obtained from
$\mathbf{s}'$ by inserting $m-j$ symbols. In both cases
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{g},\mathbf{s}')\leq|m-j|$, and therefore
\[
  d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s}')\leq d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{g})+d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{g},\mathbf{s}')
  \leq c_2+|m-j|\leq c_2+c_1\leq r. \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:Gamma}
For $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$, let
\[
  \mathcal{W}(\mathbf{x})=\big\{\mathbf{x}_{[1,j]}:\ \max\{0,m-2t\}\leq j\leq m\big\}
  \cup\big\{\mathbf{x}\mathbf{u}:\ \mathbf{u}\in\{0,1\}^{i},\ 1\leq i\leq 2t\big\},
\]
and define the \emph{projected confusion set} of $\mathbf{x}$ as
\[
  \Gamma(\mathbf{x})=\big\{\mathbf{x}'\in\{0,1\}^m\setminus\{\mathbf{x}\}:\
  d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{x}')\leq 2t\ \text{for some}\ \mathbf{w}\in\mathcal{W}(\mathbf{x})\big\}.
\]
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:projection}
Let $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}'\in\{0,1\}^m$ be distinct and
$\mathbf{z},\mathbf{z}'\in\{0,1\}^N$ with $N\geq 2t$. If
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{x}\mathbf{z},\mathbf{x}'\mathbf{z}')\leq 2t$, then
$\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Fix an alignment of $\mathbf{x}\mathbf{z}$ and $\mathbf{x}'\mathbf{z}'$ of
cost at most $2t$, and cut it right after the column containing the last
symbol of $\mathbf{x}'$ in the bottom row. By (F2), we obtain an alignment of
$\mathbf{w}=(\mathbf{x}\mathbf{z})_{[1,j]}$ and $\mathbf{x}'$ of cost
$c_1\leq 2t$ for some $j$, so that
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{x}')\leq 2t$. By (F1), $|j-m|\leq c_1\leq 2t$.
If $j\leq m$, then $\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{x}_{[1,j]}$ with $j\geq m-2t$. If
$j>m$, then $\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{x}\,\mathbf{z}_{[1,j-m]}$ with
$1\leq j-m\leq 2t\leq N$. In both cases $\mathbf{w}\in\mathcal{W}(\mathbf{x})$,
and hence $\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:Gammasize}
Suppose that $m+2t\leq n$ and $n\geq 2t+1$. Then for every
$\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$,
\[
  |\Gamma(\mathbf{x})|\leq D_t\,n^{2t},\qquad\text{where}\quad D_t=(2t+1)\,2^{8t+2}.
\]
Moreover, $\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$ can be enumerated (possibly with repetitions)
in time $O_t(n^{2t+1})$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The set $\mathcal{W}(\mathbf{x})$ contains at most
$(2t+1)+\sum_{i=1}^{2t}2^i=2t-1+2^{2t+1}\leq 2^{2t+2}$ words, each of length at
most $m+2t\leq n$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:ball} with $r=2t$, each word
$\mathbf{w}\in\mathcal{W}(\mathbf{x})$ satisfies
$|\mathcal{E}_{2t}(\mathbf{w})|\leq(2t+1)(8n)^{2t}$, and
$\mathcal{E}_{2t}(\mathbf{w})$ can be enumerated in time $O_t(n^{2t+1})$.
Therefore $|\Gamma(\mathbf{x})|\leq 2^{2t+2}(2t+1)8^{2t}n^{2t}=D_t n^{2t}$, and
$\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$ is enumerated by listing
$\mathcal{E}_{2t}(\mathbf{w})$ for all $\mathbf{w}\in\mathcal{W}(\mathbf{x})$
and keeping the words of length $m$ that differ from $\mathbf{x}$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The constant $D_t$ is far from optimized. For instance, the edit sequences
counted in Lemma~\ref{lem:ball} produce many repeated words. Since $D_t$
only affects the $O_t(1)$ term of the redundancy, we do not pursue this.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:collision}
For distinct $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}'\in\{0,1\}^m$, the number of
$a\in\mathbb{F}_q$ with $h_a(\mathbf{x})=h_a(\mathbf{x}')$ is at most
$k-1<m/b<n$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Since the block representation is injective, the polynomial
$R(Z)=P_{\mathbf{x}}(Z)-P_{\mathbf{x}'}(Z)$ is nonzero, and its degree is at
most $k-1$. A nonzero polynomial over a field has at most as many roots as
its degree, and $h_a(\mathbf{x})=h_a(\mathbf{x}')$ if and only if $R(a)=0$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:tagcode}
An \emph{$(h,N,t)$-tag code} is an injective map
$A:\{0,1\}^h\to\{0,1\}^N$ such that
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(A(\mathbf{T}),A(\mathbf{T}'))\geq 2t+1$ for all distinct
$\mathbf{T},\mathbf{T}'\in\{0,1\}^h$. Its \emph{overhead} is $N-h$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:tagcode}
Let $h\geq 1$ and $N\geq 2t+1$ satisfy $2^{N-h}\geq(2t+1)(8N)^{2t}$. Then an
$(h,N,t)$-tag code exists and can be constructed deterministically in time
$O_t(2^N N^{2t+1})$. In particular, for all sufficiently large $h$, there is
an $(h,N,t)$-tag code with overhead
\[
  \rho_t(h)=N-h=\big\lceil 2t\log(16h)+\log(2t+1)\big\rceil=2t\log h+O_t(1).
\]
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Scan $\{0,1\}^N$ in lexicographic order and select a word if its edit
distance to every previously selected word is at least $2t+1$. Let
$\mathcal{S}$ be the set of selected words. By construction, every word of
$\{0,1\}^N$ lies within distance $2t$ of some word of $\mathcal{S}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:ball}, each word of length $N\geq 2t+1$ has at most
$(2t+1)(8N)^{2t}$ words within distance $2t$, so
$|\mathcal{S}|\geq 2^N/\big((2t+1)(8N)^{2t}\big)\geq 2^h$. Let $A$ map
$\mathbf{T}$ to the $(\mathrm{val}(\mathbf{T})+1)$-th word of $\mathcal{S}$
in lexicographic order. To construct $\mathcal{S}$ efficiently, keep a Boolean
table indexed by $\{0,1\}^N$ marking the words within distance $2t$ of a
selected word; selecting a word requires marking at most
$(2t+1)(8N)^{2t}$ words, each in time $O(N)$. For the second statement, take
$N=h+\lceil 2t\log(16h)+\log(2t+1)\rceil$. For $h$ large enough we have
$N\leq 2h$, and hence $2^{N-h}\geq(2t+1)(16h)^{2t}\geq(2t+1)(8N)^{2t}$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:tagcode}
In our constructions, $h=O_t(\log n)$, so the greedy tag code is computed once
in time polynomial in $n$. Alternatively, any explicit code of minimum edit
distance at least $2t+1$ can serve as a tag code. For example, a systematic
binary $2t$-deletion correcting code is a valid tag code: if two words of
length $N$ have edit distance at most $2t$, an optimal alignment has $s$
substitutions and $i$ insertions and $i$ deletions with $s+2i\leq 2t$, so
the words share a common subsequence of length at least $N-s-i\geq N-2t$. The
systematic $2t$-deletion correcting codes of~\cite{SimaGabrysBruck2020Sys}
thus yield tag codes with overhead $8t\log h+o(\log h)$ that are encodable in
time polynomial in $h=O_t(\log n)$, which avoids the precomputation of
Lemma~\ref{lem:tagcode} at the cost of a larger $O_t(\log\log n)$ term.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:separating}
A seed $a\in\mathbb{F}_q$ \emph{separates} $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$ if
$h_a(\mathbf{x})\neq h_a(\mathbf{x}')$ for every
$\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:existsgood}
Suppose that $m+2t\leq n$, $n\geq 2t+1$, and $q\geq D_t n^{2t+1}$. Then every
$\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$ has a separating seed in $\mathbb{F}_q$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:collision}, each $\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$
collides with $\mathbf{x}$ under fewer than $n$ seeds. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:Gammasize}, the number of seeds that fail to separate
$\mathbf{x}$ is therefore less than $|\Gamma(\mathbf{x})|\cdot n\leq D_t n^{2t+1}\leq q$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- construction-1: body_md -->
\label{con:single}
Let $t\geq 1$ and let $n$ be sufficiently large. Set
\[
  b=\big\lceil\log\big(D_t n^{2t+1}\big)\big\rceil,\qquad q=2^b,\qquad
  h=2b,\qquad N=h+\rho_t(h),\qquad m=n-N,
\]
and let $A$ be an $(h,N,t)$-tag code (Lemma~\ref{lem:tagcode}). For
$\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$, define the \emph{tag}
\[
  \mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})=\mathrm{bin}_b\big(\iota(a_{\mathbf{x}})\big)\,\|\,
  \phi^{-1}\big(h_{a_{\mathbf{x}}}(\mathbf{x})\big)\ \in\{0,1\}^{2b},
\]
and the encoder
\[
  \mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{A}}:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}^n,\qquad
  \mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{A}}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{x}\,\|\,A\big(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})\big).
\]
Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{A}}=\{\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{A}}(\mathbf{x}):\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m\}$.
<!-- end construction-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:single}
For every fixed $t\geq 1$ and every sufficiently large $n$, the code
$\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{A}}$ of Construction~\ref{con:single} is a systematic
$t$-edit correcting code of length $n$ with redundancy
\[
  r_{\mathrm{A}}=N\leq(4t+2)\log n+2t\log\log n+O_t(1).
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
\emph{Correctness.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:dist}, it suffices to show that
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\geq 2t+1$ for distinct codewords
$\mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x}\,\|\,A(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}))$ and
$\mathbf{c}'=\mathbf{x}'\,\|\,A(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}'))$. Suppose to the
contrary that $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\leq 2t$. Since
$|\mathbf{x}|=|\mathbf{x}'|=m$, Lemma~\ref{lem:suffix} gives
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(A(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})),A(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}')))\leq 2t$,
and since $A$ is a tag code, $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}')$.
Hence $a_{\mathbf{x}}=a_{\mathbf{x}'}=:a$ and
$h_a(\mathbf{x})=h_a(\mathbf{x}')$. As $\mathbf{c}\neq\mathbf{c}'$, we have
$\mathbf{x}\neq\mathbf{x}'$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:projection} (with $N\geq 2t$)
yields $\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$. This contradicts the fact that $a$
separates $\mathbf{x}$.
 
\emph{Systematicity and redundancy.} The first $m$ symbols of
$\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{A}}(\mathbf{x})$ are $\mathbf{x}$, so
$\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{A}}$ is injective and systematic, and
$|\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{A}}|=2^m$. The redundancy is $n-m=N=2b+\rho_t(2b)$.
Since $b\leq(2t+1)\log n+\log D_t+1$ and
$\rho_t(2b)=2t\log b+O_t(1)=2t\log\log n+O_t(1)$, we obtain the stated bound.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:single}
The tag of Construction~\ref{con:single} has two parts of about
$(2t+1)\log n$ bits each. The hash value $h_a(\mathbf{x})$ must take about
$|\Gamma(\mathbf{x})|\cdot n\approx n^{2t+1}$ values to leave room for a
separating seed, and the seed $a$ itself is needed because the decoder does
not know which seed the encoder used. Up to the extra factor $n$, which
counts the collisions of a single competitor, this is the familiar
``twice the GV bound'' cost of syndrome compression~\cite{SimaGabrysBruck2020SC}
and of coloring-based constructions~\cite{LiGabrysFarnoud2026}: a coloring
of a graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ costs about $2\log\Delta$ bits. The
point of the next section is that the seed need not be pure redundancy.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:goodbad}
Let $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$. A hash $h_a\in\mathcal{H}_q$ (equivalently, a
seed $a\in\mathbb{F}_q$) is \emph{bad} for $\mathbf{x}$ if there exists
$\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$ with $h_a(\mathbf{x})=h_a(\mathbf{x}')$,
and \emph{good} for $\mathbf{x}$ otherwise. We write
\[
  \mathrm{Bad}(\mathbf{x})=\bigcup_{\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})}\{a\in\mathbb{F}_q:\ P_{\mathbf{x}}(a)=P_{\mathbf{x}'}(a)\},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Good}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\mathrm{Bad}(\mathbf{x}).
\]
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:bad}
If $m+2t\leq n$ and $n\geq 2t+1$, then
$|\mathrm{Bad}(\mathbf{x})|<D_t n^{2t+1}$ for every $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:collision}, each $\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$
contributes fewer than $n$ bad seeds, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:Gammasize},
$|\Gamma(\mathbf{x})|\leq D_t n^{2t}$. The claim follows from the union
bound.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:halfgood}
If, in addition, $q\geq 2D_t n^{2t+1}$, then
$|\mathrm{Good}(\mathbf{x})|>q/2$ for every $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
$|\mathrm{Good}(\mathbf{x})|=q-|\mathrm{Bad}(\mathbf{x})|>q-D_t n^{2t+1}\geq q/2$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- construction-2: body_md -->
\label{con:many}
Let $t\geq 1$ and let $n$ be sufficiently large. Set
\[
  b=\big\lceil\log\big(2D_t n^{2t+1}\big)\big\rceil,\quad q=2^b,\quad K=2^{b-1},\quad
  h=2b,\quad N=h+\rho_t(h),\quad m=n-N,
\]
and let $A$ be an $(h,N,t)$-tag code. The message set is
$\{0,1\}^{m}\times\{0,1\}^{b-1}$. For a message
$\mathbf{w}=(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\nu})$ with $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$ and
$\boldsymbol{\nu}\in\{0,1\}^{b-1}$, let $v=1+\mathrm{val}(\boldsymbol{\nu})\in[K]$,
let $a=g_{\mathbf{x},v}$, and define
\[
  \mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)=\mathrm{bin}_b\big(\iota(a)\big)\,\|\,\phi^{-1}\big(P_{\mathbf{x}}(a)\big)\in\{0,1\}^{2b},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\nu})=\mathbf{x}\,\|\,A\big(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)\big).
\]
Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{B}}$ be the image of $\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{B}}$.
<!-- end construction-2 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:tagsep}
Let $\mathbf{x}\in\{0,1\}^m$, $v,v'\in[K]$, and
$\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$. Then
$\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)\neq\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}',v')$. Moreover,
$\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)\neq\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v')$ whenever $v\neq v'$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
If $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)=\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}',v')$, then the first
halves give a common seed $a=g_{\mathbf{x},v}=g_{\mathbf{x}',v'}$, and the
second halves give $P_{\mathbf{x}}(a)=P_{\mathbf{x}'}(a)$. Since $a$ is good
for $\mathbf{x}$, this contradicts $\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$. For
the second claim, distinct ranks $v\neq v'$ give distinct seeds
$g_{\mathbf{x},v}\neq g_{\mathbf{x},v'}$, and hence distinct first halves.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:many}
For every fixed $t\geq 1$ and every sufficiently large $n$, the code
$\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{B}}$ of Construction~\ref{con:many} is a $t$-edit
correcting code of length $n$ with $|\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{B}}|=2^{m+b-1}$
and redundancy
\[
  r_{\mathrm{B}}=N-(b-1)=b+1+\rho_t(2b)\leq(2t+1)\log n+2t\log\log n+O_t(1).
\]
Moreover, the first $m=n-O_t(\log n)$ symbols of every codeword are message
symbols.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
\emph{Correctness and injectivity.} Let
$\mathbf{c}=\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\nu})$ and
$\mathbf{c}'=\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{x}',\boldsymbol{\nu}')$ with
$(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\nu})\neq(\mathbf{x}',\boldsymbol{\nu}')$, and let
$v=1+\mathrm{val}(\boldsymbol{\nu})$ and $v'=1+\mathrm{val}(\boldsymbol{\nu}')$.
We show that $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\geq 2t+1$; in particular
$\mathbf{c}\neq\mathbf{c}'$, so $\mathrm{Enc}_{\mathrm{B}}$ is injective, and
the code is $t$-edit correcting by Lemma~\ref{lem:dist}. Suppose to the
contrary that $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{c}')\leq 2t$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:suffix},
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(A(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)),A(\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}',v')))\leq 2t$,
and since $A$ is a tag code,
$\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x},v)=\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x}',v')$. If
$\mathbf{x}\neq\mathbf{x}'$, then Lemma~\ref{lem:projection} gives
$\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:tagsep}. If
$\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x}'$, then $v\neq v'$, again contradicting
Lemma~\ref{lem:tagsep}.
 
\emph{Redundancy.} The code has $2^{m+b-1}$ codewords of length
$n=m+N$, so its redundancy is $N-(b-1)=2b+\rho_t(2b)-b+1=b+1+\rho_t(2b)$.
Since $b\leq(2t+1)\log n+\log D_t+2$ and
$\rho_t(2b)=2t\log\log n+O_t(1)$, the bound follows.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Construction~\ref{con:many} uses a field that is only twice as large as that
of Construction~\ref{con:single}, i.e., one extra bit in each half of the tag,
but recycles $b-1$ bits of the seed. The leading term of the redundancy thus
drops from $2\log(D_t n^{2t+1})$ to $\log(D_t n^{2t+1})$. In both
constructions the leading term is governed by
\[
  \log\big(|\Gamma(\mathbf{x})|\cdot\text{(maximum number of collisions per competitor)}\big)
  \approx\log\big(n^{2t}\cdot n\big),
\]
and the fold removes the factor of two in front of it.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
Construction~\ref{con:many} is not fully systematic, since the $b-1$ bits of
$\boldsymbol{\nu}$ are encoded in the choice of the seed. However, the first
$m=n-O_t(\log n)$ symbols of each codeword are the message bits
$\mathbf{x}$, so the code is partial-systematic. If the tag code $A$ is itself systematic (Remark~\ref{rem:tagcode}),
the seed and the hash value also appear in the clear in the codeword.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:collision} gives fewer than $m/b$ collisions per competitor
rather than fewer than $n$, and the constant $D_t$ can be reduced. These
improvements only affect the $O_t(\log\log n)$ and $O_t(1)$ terms, and we do
not pursue them here.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:roots}
Algorithm~\ref{alg:roots} returns all roots of $R$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$ using
$O(b^2d^2)$ operations in $\mathbb{F}_q$. In particular, if $d<k$, it uses
$O(n^2)$ operations in $\mathbb{F}_q$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Since $Z^q-Z=\prod_{a\in\mathbb{F}_q}(Z-a)$ is squarefree, $G$ is the product
of $Z-r$ over the distinct roots $r$ of $R$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$. For every such
root $r$, $T_i(r)=\mathrm{Tr}(\beta_ir)\in\{0,1\}$, so each factor $F$ of $G$
is the product of $\gcd(F,T_i)$ and $\gcd(F,T_i+1)$, which collect the roots
of $F$ with $\mathrm{Tr}(\beta_ir)=0$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(\beta_ir)=1$,
respectively. If $r\neq r'$ are two roots, then
$\mathrm{Tr}(\beta_i(r-r'))\neq 0$ for some $i$, since otherwise
$\mathrm{Tr}(y(r-r'))=0$ for all $y\in\mathbb{F}_q$, contradicting the
nondegeneracy of the trace form. Hence, after the loop, all factors in
$\mathcal{F}$ are linear and correspond to the distinct roots of $R$.
 
For the complexity, computing $S$ takes $b$ squarings modulo $R$, i.e.,
$O(bd^2)$ operations, and the gcd takes $O(d^2)$ operations. Let
$e=\deg G\leq d$. Each $T_i$ is obtained by $b$ squarings modulo $G$ in
$O(be^2)$ operations, and the gcds in iteration $i$ cost $O(e^2)$ operations
in total, since the degrees of the factors in $\mathcal{F}$ sum to $e$. Over
the $b$ iterations, this gives $O(bd^2+b^2e^2)=O(b^2d^2)$ operations. If
$d<k\leq n/b+1$, this is $O(n^2)$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:badcost}
Algorithm~\ref{alg:bad} computes $\mathrm{Bad}(\mathbf{x})$ using
$O_t(n^{2t+2})$ operations in $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $O_t(n^{2t+1}\log n)$
additional bit operations, i.e., $O_t(n^{2t+2}\log^2 n)$ bit operations in
total. Given its output, \textsc{Select} and \textsc{Rank} take
$O_t(n^{2t+1}\log n)$ bit operations.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Gammasize}, \textsc{EnumGamma} takes $O_t(n^{2t+1})$ time
and returns at most $D_tn^{2t}$ words. For each of them, forming
$P_{\mathbf{x}}-P_{\mathbf{x}'}$ takes $O(n)$ bit operations and $O(k)$ field
operations, and Lemma~\ref{lem:roots} gives $O(n^2)$ field operations for the
roots. The list $\mathcal{B}$ has fewer than $D_tn^{2t+1}$ entries before
removing repetitions (Lemma~\ref{lem:bad}), and sorting it takes
$O_t(n^{2t+1}\log n)$ comparisons of $b$-bit integers. The scan for
\textsc{Select} and the binary search for \textsc{Rank} are linear and
logarithmic in $|\mathcal{B}|$, respectively.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:deccorrect}
Let $\mathbf{c}=\mathbf{x}\,\|\,A(\mathbf{T})$ be a codeword of
Construction~\ref{con:single} or~\ref{con:many} with tag
$\mathbf{T}=\mathrm{bin}_b(\iota(a))\,\|\,\phi^{-1}(P_{\mathbf{x}}(a))$, and let
$\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{c})$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] there is $j^*\in[m-t,m+t]$ such that
    $(j^*,\mathbf{T})\in\mathcal{T}$ and
    $\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{y}_{[1,j^*]})$;
  \item[(ii)] every pair $(\mathbf{x}',\mathbf{T}')$ that passes the test in
    Step~2 satisfies $\mathbf{x}'=\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{T}'=\mathbf{T}$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, Algorithm~\ref{alg:dec} outputs the message encoded by
$\mathbf{c}$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
(i) Fix an alignment of $\mathbf{c}$ and $\mathbf{y}$ of cost at most $t$ and
cut it right after the column containing $c_m$, the last symbol of
$\mathbf{x}$. By (F2), we obtain an alignment of $\mathbf{x}$ and
$\mathbf{y}_{[1,j^*]}$ of cost $c_1$ and an alignment of $A(\mathbf{T})$ and
$\mathbf{y}_{[j^*+1,|\mathbf{y}|]}$ of cost $c_2$, with $c_1+c_2\leq t$. By
(F1), $|j^*-m|\leq c_1\leq t$. Hence
$\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{y}_{[1,j^*]})$ and
$A(\mathbf{T})\in\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{y}_{[j^*+1,|\mathbf{y}|]})$, so
$(j^*,\mathbf{T})$ is added to $\mathcal{T}$ in Step~1. In particular, the
true payload $\mathbf{x}$ passes the test of Step~2 for $(j^*,\mathbf{T})$,
since $P_{\mathbf{x}}(a)=\beta$ and
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{y})\leq t$.
 
(ii) Suppose that $\mathbf{x}'\in\{0,1\}^m$ and
$\mathbf{T}'=\mathrm{bin}_b(\iota(a'))\,\|\,\phi^{-1}(\beta')$ pass the test,
i.e., $P_{\mathbf{x}'}(a')=\beta'$ and the word
$\mathbf{c}''=\mathbf{x}'\,\|\,A(\mathbf{T}')$ satisfies
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c}'',\mathbf{y})\leq t$. Note that $\mathbf{c}''$ need
not be a codeword a priori. By the triangle inequality,
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{c}'',\mathbf{c})\leq 2t$. Lemma~\ref{lem:suffix} gives
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(A(\mathbf{T}'),A(\mathbf{T}))\leq 2t$, so
$\mathbf{T}'=\mathbf{T}$ because $A$ is a tag code; thus $a'=a$ and
$P_{\mathbf{x}'}(a)=\beta=P_{\mathbf{x}}(a)$. If $\mathbf{x}'\neq\mathbf{x}$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:projection} applied to $\mathbf{c}$ and $\mathbf{c}''$ gives
$\mathbf{x}'\in\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$, contradicting the fact that $a$ is good
for $\mathbf{x}$. Hence $\mathbf{x}'=\mathbf{x}$.
 
By (i) and (ii), after Step~2 we have $(\hat{\mathbf{x}},\hat a)=(\mathbf{x},a)$.
For Construction~\ref{con:single}, the message is $\mathbf{x}$. For
Construction~\ref{con:many}, $a=g_{\mathbf{x},v}$, where
$v=1+\mathrm{val}(\boldsymbol{\nu})$, so
$\textsc{Rank}_{\mathbf{x}}(a)=v$ and the output is $(\mathbf{x},\boldsymbol{\nu})$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:complexity}
Let $t\geq 1$ be fixed, and assume the precomputation above. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[(a)] The encoders of Constructions~\ref{con:single}
    and~\ref{con:many} use $O_t(n^{2t+2})$ operations in $\mathbb{F}_q$,
    i.e., $O_t(n^{2t+2}\log^2 n)$ bit operations.
  \item[(b)] The decoder of Construction~\ref{con:single} uses
    $O_t(n^{t+1}\log n)$ bit operations.
  \item[(c)] The decoder of Construction~\ref{con:many} uses
    $O_t(n^{2t+2}\log^2n)$ bit operations, dominated by a single call to
    \textsc{BadSet}.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
(a) The encoder calls \textsc{BadSet} and \textsc{Select} once
(Lemma~\ref{lem:badcost}), evaluates $P_{\mathbf{x}}$ at one point with $O(k)$
field operations, and calls $A$ once.
 
(b) In Step~1, there are at most $2t+1$ values of $j$. For each of them,
$|\mathbf{y}_{[j+1,|\mathbf{y}|]}|\leq N+2t$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:ball} the
ball $\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{y}_{[j+1,|\mathbf{y}|]})$ has
$O_t(N^t)=O_t(\log^t n)$ elements, each tested in time $\tau_A$. Since two
distinct words of the image of $A$ are at distance at least $2t+1$, each $j$
contributes at most one tag, so $|\mathcal{T}|\leq 2t+1$. In Step~2, for each
tag, the ball $\mathcal{E}_t(\mathbf{y}_{[1,j]})$ has at most
$(t+1)(8n)^t$ elements (Lemma~\ref{lem:ball}), and is enumerated in time
$O_t(n^{t+1})$. For each candidate $\mathbf{x}'$, evaluating
$P_{\mathbf{x}'}(a)$ by Horner's rule takes $O(k)=O(n/\log n)$ field
operations, i.e., $O(n\log n)$ bit operations, and deciding whether
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathbf{x}'\,\|\,A(\mathbf{T}),\mathbf{y})\leq t$ takes
$O(tn)$ time with the banded dynamic program for the edit
distance~\cite{Ukkonen1985}. In total, Step~2 takes $O_t(n^{t+1}\log n)$ bit
operations, which dominates Step~1.
 
(c) In addition to (b), the decoder of Construction~\ref{con:many} calls
\textsc{BadSet} and \textsc{Rank} once, which by Lemma~\ref{lem:badcost} costs
$O_t(n^{2t+2}\log^2 n)$ bit operations.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
With fast polynomial arithmetic, the cost of Algorithm~\ref{alg:roots}
drops from $O(b^2d^2)$ to $\tilde O(b^2d)=\tilde O(n)$ operations in
$\mathbb{F}_q$, so that \textsc{BadSet}, and hence the encoders and the
decoder of Construction~\ref{con:many}, run in $\tilde O_t(n^{2t+1})$ time.
The cost of these algorithms is dominated by the need to list all
$\Theta_t(n^{2t})$ competitors in $\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$; reducing it, for
example by exploiting the structure of the difference polynomials, is left
for future work.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
The only step of Algorithm~\ref{alg:dec} that requires
$\mathrm{Bad}(\hat{\mathbf{x}})$ is the computation of the rank of $\hat a$.
If the application only needs the payload $\mathbf{x}$, which contains all
but $b-1=O_t(\log n)$ message bits, then the decoder of
Construction~\ref{con:many} also runs in $O_t(n^{t+1}\log n)$ bit
operations.
